name: endpoints
summary: Inbound event fabric. REST listeners + webhook receivers ingest external events, EndpointRegistry catalogs them, RoutingOperator matches each event against rules and dispatches the right action (forward, reply, broadcast, log, notify, chain).
engine_pattern: abstract base.Endpoint (start/stop/receive/health) + registry pattern mirroring model_registry. Rules evaluated in priority order; first match wins.

inbound_callers: CLI: python3 endpoints_cli.py start | stop | list | status | sync | route-add | route-list | route-test | route-archive
External clients hitting REST endpoints / webhook URLs
outbound_calls: RoutingOperator → action=chain: invokes cc chat <prompt> (the MoE gateway)
RoutingOperator → action=log: appends to crystal chain via inference_logger
RoutingOperator → action=forward: re-dispatches to another endpoint
routing_connections.substrate_writes: appends event logs; updates per-endpoint health JSONs

merge_with_moe_stack: When a route action is 'chain', the inbound event becomes the prompt to cc chat full. That call flows through the entire MoE-by-retrieval pipeline (user_graph predict → MoE retrieve → enhance → route → project → log → record) just like any human-typed prompt. External webhooks effectively become first-class participants in the crystal chain.
guarantees: Deterministic rule evaluation: same event + same ruleset → same action
Crystal-chained: action=chain or action=log writes through inference_logger
Disposable listeners: start/stop is idempotent; missing configs return clean errors
usage_example: python3 core/lib/endpoints_cli.py start --kind webhook --name github_push --port 8090\npython3 core/lib/endpoints_cli.py route-add --name 'gh_to_chain' --priority 10 --match-kind webhook --match-service github_push --action chain --template 'review PR {payload.number}'
